hypotheses.reasoning: Every crash is on the same message, msg-453808 at offset 495220, with the same error: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in expandReferences. That points to a self-referencing or deeply nested payload causing runaway recursion. The worker's offset is never committed past this message, so each restart resumes at 495220 (#240, #246, #264, #292) and crashes again within seconds. The crash still happens after restarts that log v3.4.1 (#239, #245, #263), so it does not depend on the code version. Other services log no errors.

v4.20.8 rolled out at 04:41:40 and the first crash came about a minute later. But the new build processed batches without trouble (#222, #233), and restarts reporting v3.4.1 still crash on the same message. So the deploy is most likely a coincidence, or at most made the worker more fragile.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-453808 (offset 495220) on notifications.outbound to a dead-letter queue, or skip past it, so the worker can resume and work off the lag. Then look at the payload for circular or self-referencing template references. Fix expandReferences to detect cycles and cap recursion depth, and wrap per-message processing so a bad message goes to the DLQ instead of crashing the process.
